name: France
lead: Go in spring, April to June, or September to early October, for mild days, blooming parks and thinner crowds. Summer is warm and busy, and winter is cool and quiet beyond the festive season.

bestFor.p: April to June and September, with comfortable temperatures, blooming gardens and manageable lines.
June and September for warm seas without the peak August crush along the Cote d'Azur.
September and October, around the grape harvest, when the vineyards turn gold and the cellars are busy.
December to April in the Alps, with the most reliable snow in January and February.

whatsOn.p: Paris parks and the chestnut trees come into leaf, and the city is at its most photogenic.
The vendange fills the wine regions, from Bordeaux to Burgundy, with activity and colour.

name: Spain
lead: Go in April to June or September to October for warm, comfortable weather and lighter crowds. July and August are hot, especially inland, and winter is mild on the coast but cool in the centre.

bestFor.p: April to June and September to October for Madrid, Barcelona and Seville, with warm days and manageable crowds.
June and September along the Mediterranean, with warm seas before and after the August peak.
Spring for Holy Week processions and Seville's April Fair, two of the country's great spectacles.
The Canary Islands and the southern coast stay mild through winter, a warm escape from northern Europe.

whatsOn.p: Semana Santa processions and Seville's Feria fill the spring calendar across the south.
Warm seas and long days on the Mediterranean, on either side of the August crowds.

name: Italy
lead: Go in spring, April to June, or September to October, for warm, dry days and thinner crowds. July and August are hot and packed, and winter is cool and quiet, ideal for art cities without the queues.

bestFor.p: April to June and September to October for Rome, Florence and Venice, with warm days and shorter queues.
June and September for the Amalfi Coast, Sardinia and Sicily, with warm seas and fewer crowds than August.
September and October bring the grape and olive harvests, truffle season and a calendar of food festivals.
December to March in the Dolomites and the northern Alps.

whatsOn.p: Wildflowers across Tuscany and Umbria, and warm, clear days in the art cities.
The vendemmia and olive harvest fill the countryside with festivals and new wine.

name: United Kingdom
lead: Aim for April to June and September, when days are mild, long and at their driest. July and August are warmest but busiest, and winter is grey and short on daylight, though rarely freezing.

bestFor.p: May and June, when the gardens bloom, the hedgerows are green and the days are long.
April to June and September, with comfortable temperatures and lighter crowds than high summer.
July and August for the warmest weather and the busy festival calendar, from Edinburgh to the seaside.
January to March, outside the holidays, when the weather is cool and damp but hotels are cheap.

whatsOn.p: The countryside turns green and the great gardens, from Kew to the Cotswolds, hit their stride.
Cities glow with Christmas lights and markets despite the short, grey days.

name: Germany
lead: Go from May to September for the mildest weather and long days. Late September is Oktoberfest, and late November to December is Christmas-market season. Winter is cold and grey beyond the markets.

bestFor.p: May, June and September, with mild weather, long days and lighter crowds than high summer.
Mid September to early October in Munich. Book accommodation across Bavaria two to three months ahead.
Late November through December, when squares from Nuremberg to Cologne fill with stalls and mulled wine.
July and August for the warmest mountain weather and open high trails in the south.

whatsOn.p: Munich fills its beer tents for the world's biggest folk festival, running into early October.
City squares across the country become glowing markets from late November.

name: Greece
lead: Go in May and June or September and October for warm, dry days, swimmable seas and lighter crowds. July and August are hot and packed, and winter is mild but many islands wind down.

bestFor.p: Late May to mid June and September, with warm seas, sunshine and fewer crowds than the August rush.
April, May, June, September and October, when Athens and Delphi are pleasant rather than scorching.
July and August, when Mykonos and the party islands are at full tilt.
May and October bring the best mix of good weather, open tavernas and cheaper rates.

whatsOn.p: Ferries run, tavernas open and the Aegean warms up for swimming.
The sea is at its warmest after a summer of sun, ideal for late swimming.

name: Portugal
lead: Go in March to May or September to October for warm, sunny days and fewer crowds. July and August are hot and busy on the coast, and winter is mild but changeable.

bestFor.p: March to May and September to October for Lisbon and Porto, with warm days and lighter crowds.
June and September in the Algarve, with warm seas on either side of the August peak.
Autumn brings the biggest Atlantic swells to spots like Nazare and the western coast.
September in the Douro Valley, around the grape harvest, with golden terraces above the river.

whatsOn.p: The city's saint's-day festivals peak around St Anthony on 13 June, with street parties across the old quarters.
The port-wine vineyards come alive for the vintage along the river valleys.

name: Netherlands
lead: Go in spring, April to May, for the tulips, or summer, June to August, for the longest, mildest days. The weather is changeable year round, so pack a layer and an umbrella whenever you come.

bestFor.p: Mid April for the peak of the bulb fields and Keukenhof, the single most popular time to visit.
May to September for warm, long days exploring Amsterdam and the countryside by bike.
King's Day in late April and the summer months, when the cities fill with open-air events.
Autumn and winter, outside the holidays, for cheaper, quieter, atmospheric city breaks.

whatsOn.p: The bulb fields and Keukenhof gardens burst into colour for a few short weeks.
The whole country turns orange for one of Europe's biggest street parties.

name: Switzerland
lead: Go in summer, June to September, for hiking, lakes and open mountain passes, or in winter, December to March, for skiing. The quiet shoulder seasons are cheaper but some lifts and trails close.

bestFor.p: July and August, when the trails are clear of snow, the cable cars run and the meadows are in full flower.
December to March across the Alpine resorts, with the deepest, most reliable snow at altitude.
June to September for warm days, lake swimming and the long light of an Alpine summer.
Late spring and autumn for fewer crowds and better rates, accepting that some high lifts and trails may be shut.

whatsOn.p: Wildflower meadows, open trails and warm lakes across the mountains.
The resorts fill with snow for some of the world's finest skiing.

name: Iceland
lead: Go in summer, June to August, for the mildest weather, open highland roads and the midnight sun. For the northern lights, come September to March, when the nights are long and dark but the weather is harsh.

bestFor.p: June to August, when all roads are open, the weather is mildest and the days are endless.
September to March, on clear, dark nights away from town. October, February and March balance aurora odds with manageable conditions.
June and July, when the sun barely sets and you can hike or drive late into the night.
May and September are quieter shoulders with a chance of both decent weather and early or late auroras.

whatsOn.p: Near round-the-clock daylight opens up long evenings of hiking and driving.
Dark, clear nights give the best chance of the aurora dancing overhead.

name: Norway
lead: Go in summer, June to August, for the fjords, hiking and the midnight sun. For the northern lights, come late September to March, when the northern nights are long and dark. Winter is cold, but the aurora makes up for it.

bestFor.p: June to August for the warmest, longest days, open mountain roads and every ferry and cable car running.
Late September to March in the Arctic north around Tromso, on clear, dark nights away from town.
June and July above the Arctic Circle, when the sun never fully sets.
December to March, deep in the snowy winter, across the mountains and the north.

whatsOn.p: Above the Arctic Circle the sun stays up around the clock, opening endless summer days.
The aurora dances over the Arctic north on clear winter nights.

name: Sweden
lead: Go in summer, June to August, for warm, near-endless days, the Stockholm archipelago and midsummer. Winter, December to March, brings the northern lights, dog-sledding and snow in Lapland, though the south stays dark and cold.

bestFor.p: June to August for warm days, long light and the islands at their liveliest.
Late June, Sweden's biggest celebration, with maypoles, flowers and parties under the midnight sun.
December to March in Lapland, on clear, dark nights away from the cities.
May and September, mild shoulder months with fewer crowds and softer prices.

whatsOn.p: The whole country celebrates the longest days with maypoles and feasting.
The aurora dances over Swedish Lapland on clear winter nights.

name: Croatia
lead: Go in May to June or September to October for warm seas, sunshine and far fewer crowds than the July to August peak. Winter is mild on the coast but quiet, with many islands winding down.

bestFor.p: June and September for warm seas and sunshine on the Dalmatian coast, on either side of the August peak.
May to June and September to October for comfortable sightseeing without the cruise-day crush.
Late spring to early autumn, when the seas are warm and the harbours less frantic than midsummer.
Spring for full waterfalls after the snowmelt, or autumn for golden colour and fewer visitors.

whatsOn.p: Warm Adriatic water and long days, with the shoulder months calmer than August.
Dubrovnik and the coastal towns host open-air music and theatre under warm night skies.

name: Turkey
lead: Go in spring, April to May, or autumn, September to October, for warm, comfortable days and lighter crowds. Summer is hot and busy on the coast, and winter is cool, with skiing inland.

bestFor.p: April to May and September to October for comfortable sightseeing and the Bosphorus at its best.
Spring and autumn for the calmest, clearest mornings for hot-air ballooning over the valleys.
June to September on the Turquoise Coast, or the warm shoulder months to dodge the peak heat.
November and the early spring bring cooler weather, quiet sites and better value.

whatsOn.p: Istanbul's parks fill with millions of tulips, the flower's historic home.
The Aegean and Mediterranean shores are warm, sunny and made for swimming.

name: Ireland
lead: Go from May to September for the mildest weather, the longest days and the greenest scenery. There is no dry season, so showers are likely any month, but spring and summer give the best odds of bright spells.

bestFor.p: June to August for the Wild Atlantic Way, with the longest days and the best chance of clear skies.
May to September for Dublin, Galway and Cork, with mild weather and lively festivals.
Late spring, when the countryside is at its greenest after the winter rains.
Autumn and winter, outside the holidays, for cheaper, atmospheric trips with fewer crowds.

whatsOn.p: The whole island, and Dublin especially, throws its biggest celebration in mid March.
Around midsummer the light lingers past 10pm, perfect for the coast and the countryside.

name: Austria
lead: Go in summer, June to September, for hiking, the lakes and the cities, or in winter, December to March, for skiing and Christmas markets. The quiet shoulder seasons are mild and cheaper.

bestFor.p: May to September for Vienna and Salzburg, with warm days and a full calendar of music and festivals.
December to March in Tyrol and the western Alps, with the most reliable snow at altitude.
June to September for the Salzkammergut lakes and the Alpine trails in full flower.
Late November through December, when Vienna, Salzburg and Innsbruck glow with stalls and mulled wine.

whatsOn.p: Lakes, wildflower meadows and open mountain trails across the country.
Vienna and Salzburg fill their squares with festive stalls and lights.

name: Czechia
lead: Go in April to June or September to October for mild weather and thinner crowds in Prague. Summer is warm and busy, and winter is cold, but the Christmas markets and snow on the spires earn it.

bestFor.p: April to June and September to October for mild days and lighter crowds on the bridge and in the castle.
December, when Old Town Square fills with stalls, carols and mulled wine under the snow.
Summer, when the beer gardens are open and the festival calendar is full.
Late autumn and winter, outside the markets, for cheap, atmospheric, crowd-free city breaks.

whatsOn.p: Prague's parks and palace gardens come into bloom under mild skies.
Old Town Square glows with festive stalls and a towering tree.

name: Poland
lead: Go from May to September for the mildest weather and longest days across Krakow, Warsaw and the lakes. Winter is cold and snowy, with Christmas markets in the cities and skiing in the Tatra Mountains.

bestFor.p: May to September for warm, long days and a full calendar, or December for the Christmas markets.
June to August for Gdansk and the beaches, the warmest, sunniest stretch on the coast.
Summer for the mountain trails around Zakopane, with skiing in the same hills in winter.
Spring and autumn, with mild weather, golden colour and better rates than the summer peak.

whatsOn.p: Krakow and Gdansk fill their old-town squares with cafes and street life.
Krakow's main square hosts one of central Europe's prettiest festive markets.

name: Morocco
lead: Go in spring, March to May, or autumn, September to November, for warm, comfortable days across the cities, the desert and the mountains. Summer is fiercely hot inland, and winter is cool, with snow on the High Atlas.

bestFor.p: March to May and September to November for warm, comfortable days in Marrakech, Fez and Chefchaouen.
October to April, avoiding the searing summer, for camel treks and nights under the desert sky.
April to June and September to October, when the trails are clear of snow and the valleys are green.
Summer on the Atlantic, where Essaouira stays cool and windy while the interior overheats.

whatsOn.p: The Sahara is comfortable from October to April, prime time for dune camps.
The Atlas foothills and the Ourika Valley turn green and blossom-filled.

name: Egypt
lead: Go in the cooler months, October to April, for comfortable days at the pyramids, on the Nile and around the temples. Summer, May to September, is intensely hot, especially in the south at Luxor and Aswan.

bestFor.p: October to April for comfortable days at Giza, Luxor and Aswan and on the river cruises.
Pleasant year round, with spring and autumn offering warm water and comfortable air temperatures.
October, November and March, the shoulder months, balance good weather with thinner crowds than the winter peak.
The cooler months, when the Western Desert and the oases are comfortable to explore.

whatsOn.p: The comfortable window for the pyramids, the Nile temples and the desert.

whatsOn.h: Abu Simbel sun festival, Feb and Oct
whatsOn.p: Twice a year the sunrise lights the inner sanctuary of the great temple.

name: South Africa
lead: For Cape Town and the coast, go in summer, November to March. For safari in Kruger, the dry winter, May to September, is best for spotting wildlife. The seasons are reversed from the northern hemisphere.

bestFor.p: May to September, the dry winter, when thin bush and busy waterholes make for the best game viewing in Kruger.
November to March for warm, dry summer days on Table Mountain, the beaches and the wine estates.
July to November along the southern coast around Hermanus, when southern right whales calve close to shore.
August and September on the West Coast, when the spring blooms carpet the Namaqualand desert.

whatsOn.p: Southern right whales gather close to the southern Cape coast to calve.
The West Coast and Namaqualand erupt in spring colour.

name: Kenya
lead: Go in the dry seasons, June to October and January to February, for the best safari game viewing, with the Great Migration reaching the Masai Mara from July to October. The long rains fall March to May, with shorter rains in November.

bestFor.p: July to October in the Masai Mara, when the wildebeest herds and dramatic river crossings arrive.
The dry seasons, June to October and January to February, for the easiest game viewing across the parks.
December to March on the coast around Diani and Mombasa, the sunniest, driest stretch.
The wet months, when migratory birds arrive and the landscapes are green, in exchange for muddier roads.

whatsOn.p: Wildebeest pour into the Masai Mara and brave the crocodile-filled river crossings.
The Indian Ocean beaches around Diani are at their sunniest and calmest.

name: Tanzania
lead: Go in the dry season, June to October, for the best safari and Serengeti game viewing. The wildebeest calving is January to February, and Zanzibar is best June to October and December to February. The long rains fall March to May.

bestFor.p: June to October for the dry-season game viewing, with river crossings in the north around August and September.
January and February on the southern Serengeti plains, when hundreds of thousands of calves are born.
June to October and December to February for sunny, dry days on the spice island.
The dry windows of January to mid March and June to October for the clearest, safest ascents.

whatsOn.p: Wildlife gathers at the water across the Serengeti and Ngorongoro.
The spice island's beaches are at their sunniest and driest.

name: United Arab Emirates
lead: Go in the cooler months, November to March, for warm, sunny days perfect for the beach, the desert and the outdoor sights. Summer, June to September, brings brutal heat and humidity, best spent indoors.

bestFor.p: November to March for warm, sunny days on the beach and out exploring Dubai and Abu Dhabi.
The cool season, when dune drives and overnight desert camps are comfortable rather than scorching.
Winter, when the calendar fills with festivals, sport and the big shopping events.
The summer months, hot but heavily discounted, for cheap luxury hotels and empty attractions.

whatsOn.p: The comfortable window for the beach, the desert and the outdoor city.
Shopping festivals, sport and concerts fill the cool-season calendar.

name: Israel
lead: Go in spring, March to May, or autumn, September to November, for warm, comfortable days across Jerusalem, Tel Aviv and the desert. Summer is hot and humid on the coast, and winter is mild but rainy.

bestFor.p: March to May and September to November for warm, comfortable days exploring on foot.
Late spring and early autumn for warm sea and sunshine without the peak summer humidity.
The shoulder months and winter, when the south is warm and dry while the coast cools.
Warm and sunny much of the year, a winter sun and diving escape.

whatsOn.p: Wildflowers carpet the Galilee and the northern hills.
Warm Mediterranean seas on either side of the humid summer peak.

name: Jordan
lead: Go in spring, March to May, or autumn, September to November, for warm, comfortable days at Petra, Wadi Rum and Amman. Summer is intensely hot in the desert, and winter is cool, with cold nights and the odd snowfall in Amman.

bestFor.p: March to May and September to November for comfortable, sunny days exploring the rose-red city on foot.
Spring and autumn for warm days and clear desert nights ideal for camping under the stars.

bestFor.h: The Dead Sea and Red Sea
bestFor.p: The shoulder months and even winter for warm water without the summer desert heat.
Spring, when the desert briefly greens and wildflowers appear, or mild autumn.

whatsOn.p: The prime windows for walking Petra and camping in Wadi Rum.
The Treasury glows under candlelight on select evenings through the year.

name: Japan
lead: Go in spring, late March to May, for cherry blossom and mild days, or in November for crisp air and red maple leaves. Avoid August to October, which is hot, wet and typhoon-prone.

bestFor.p: Late March to mid April in Tokyo and Kyoto, reaching Hokkaido in early May. It lasts only a week or two in any one place, so book months ahead.
November across most of Honshu. Kyoto temples and the mountains around Nikko are spectacular, and a touch quieter than spring.
January and February for the lightest powder in Hokkaido and the Japan Alps. The deep cold keeps the snow famously dry.
January, early February and the rainy stretch of June bring the lowest prices and thinnest crowds, in exchange for cold or damp weather.

whatsOn.h: Cherry blossom, late Mar to May
whatsOn.p: The country pauses for hanami, blossom-viewing picnics under the trees in parks and along riversides.
Koyo lights up temple gardens and mountain valleys in red and gold.

name: China
lead: Go in spring, April to May, or autumn, September to October, for the mildest, driest weather. Summer is hot and humid, and winter is cold, especially in the north. Avoid the national holiday crowds in early May and October.

bestFor.p: September and October for clear skies and comfortable days, or spring before the summer heat.
April to May and September to October for Beijing, Xi'an and Shanghai at their most pleasant.
Spring and autumn, with the gorges most atmospheric and the weather mild on the river.
The shoulder weeks outside the May and October national holidays, when the big sights are far quieter.

whatsOn.p: Cherry and plum blossom open across the parks and the southern gardens.
The Great Wall and the northern hills turn gold under clear blue skies.

name: India
lead: Go in the cool, dry season, October to March, for the most comfortable weather. April to June brings fierce heat, and the monsoon, July to September, brings the rains. The Himalaya and the far south follow their own rhythm.

bestFor.p: October to March for Delhi, Agra and Jaipur, with comfortable days for sightseeing.
November to March in Goa and Kerala, the warm, dry window on the southern coasts.
June to September for trekking in Ladakh, Spiti and the mountain valleys.
March to May, when the heat draws wildlife to the waterholes in the central national parks.

whatsOn.p: The festival of colour erupts across the north at the end of winter.
The festival of lights fills cities and homes with lamps, fireworks and feasting.

name: Thailand
lead: Go in the cool, dry season, November to February, for the most comfortable weather. March to May is fiercely hot, and the monsoon runs roughly June to October, though the islands differ coast to coast.

bestFor.p: November to April on the Andaman coast for Phuket and Krabi, with calm, clear seas and sunshine.
November to February for Bangkok and Chiang Mai, with the year's most comfortable weather.
Songkran, the water-fight new year, in April, and Loy Krathong, the festival of lights, in November.
June to October brings cheaper travel and green landscapes, with rain that often falls in short bursts.

whatsOn.p: The Thai new year turns the whole country into a giant, joyful water fight.
Floating lanterns and candle-lit baskets drift on rivers and lakes across the country.

name: Vietnam
lead: For the whole country at once, go in spring, March to April, or autumn, October to November. The north suits October to April, the centre February to August, and the south is warm and dry from December to April.

bestFor.p: March to April and October to November, the shoulder months when no region is at its worst.
October to April for cooler, clearer days, avoiding the summer storms on the bay.
February to August for Hoi An, Da Nang and Nha Trang, before the autumn rains arrive.
December to April, the southern dry season, for easy travel and sunny days.

whatsOn.p: Mild, golden weather makes the capital and the northern mountains at their most photogenic.

whatsOn.h: Central beach season, Mar to Aug
whatsOn.p: Hoi An and Da Nang enjoy their driest, sunniest stretch.

name: Indonesia
lead: Go in the dry season, April to October, for sunny days, calm seas and the best diving. The wet season, November to March, brings warm afternoon downpours, cheaper stays and green landscapes.

bestFor.p: April to October for the clearest water and calmest seas around Bali, Komodo and Raja Ampat.
May to September for the classic dry-season swells on the Bukit Peninsula and beyond.
The dry season for clear sunrises over Bromo and Ijen and firmer trails.
November to March brings better rates, fewer crowds and emerald rice terraces, in exchange for daily rain.

whatsOn.p: Bali falls silent for its day of silence, a striking and uniquely Balinese new year.
Sunny days and calm seas across the islands, at their busiest in July and August.

name: Nepal
lead: Go in autumn, October to November, for the clearest mountain views and the best trekking, or spring, March to April, for warm days and the rhododendron bloom. The monsoon brings rain and cloud from June to September.

bestFor.p: October to November for the clearest, most stable conditions, or March to April for warmer days and blooms.
Autumn, when the post-monsoon air is at its clearest and the peaks are razor sharp.
March and April, when the forests of the middle hills burst into red and pink.
October to March, the cooler dry months, for rhinos and tigers in the lowland jungle.

whatsOn.p: The post-monsoon skies make autumn the sharpest time to see the Himalaya.
The hill forests light up in March and April along the trekking routes.

name: Sri Lanka
lead: Go in December to March for the west and south coasts, including the beaches around Galle and the cultural sites. The east coast, including Trincomalee and Arugam Bay, is best from May to September. Two monsoons split the island.

bestFor.p: December to March for the sands around Galle, Mirissa and Unawatuna at their sunniest.
May to September for Trincomalee, Pasikuda and the famous waves at Arugam Bay.
The drier months at each park, with Yala best from February to July and superb leopard spotting.
December to April off Mirissa in the south, when blue whales pass close to shore.

whatsOn.p: Blue and sperm whales pass the south coast off Mirissa.

whatsOn.h: East coast season, May to Sep
whatsOn.p: Trincomalee and Arugam Bay enjoy their sunny, dry window.

name: Philippines
lead: Go in the dry season, December to May, for sunny days and calm seas across the islands. The wet season, June to November, brings the rains and overlaps the typhoon season, which peaks from July to October.

bestFor.p: January to April for Boracay, Palawan and the Visayas, the driest, sunniest, calmest stretch.
The dry season for clear water, with Tubbataha Reef open only from March to June.
Roughly November to May off Donsol and the southern islands, in the calmer dry months.
June, before the worst of the storms, for cheaper travel and greener landscapes.

whatsOn.p: The islands enjoy their sunniest, calmest weather, peaking around Easter.

whatsOn.h: Whale shark season, Nov to May
whatsOn.p: Whale sharks gather off Donsol and the southern coasts.

name: Malaysia
lead: Malaysia is warm and humid all year. The west coast and islands (Langkawi, Penang) are driest from December to March, while the east coast (the Perhentians, Tioman) is best from March to October and closes for the monsoon in winter.

bestFor.p: December to March for Langkawi and Penang, the driest, sunniest stretch on that side.
March to October for the Perhentians and Tioman, with calm, clear water for snorkelling and diving.
Year round in Kuala Lumpur and Penang, where the rain comes in bursts and the eating never stops.
Drier months from March to October for Sabah, orangutans and Mount Kinabalu.

whatsOn.h: West coast dry season, Dec to Mar
whatsOn.p: Langkawi and Penang enjoy their sunniest, calmest beach weather.

whatsOn.h: East coast diving, Mar to Oct
whatsOn.p: The Perhentian and Tioman reefs open up with clear, calm seas.

name: South Korea
lead: Go in spring, April to June, for cherry blossom, or autumn, September to November, for crisp air and golden foliage. Summer is hot, humid and wet, and winter is cold and dry, with skiing.

bestFor.p: Late March to mid April, sweeping north from Jeju to Seoul, lighting up parks and palace grounds.
Late October to early November, when the mountains and city parks turn red and gold.
December to February in the Gangwon mountains, on the slopes that hosted the Winter Olympics.
May to June and September to October, the mild, dry shoulders, for the national parks.

whatsOn.p: Festivals bloom across the country, from Jinhae in the south to Seoul's palaces.
Maples and ginkgoes set the mountains and temple grounds alight.

name: Cambodia
lead: Go in the cool, dry season, November to February, for the most comfortable weather at Angkor Wat and beyond. March to May is intensely hot, and the wet season, June to October, brings afternoon downpours and a green landscape.

bestFor.p: November to February for cool mornings, clear skies and the most comfortable temple-hopping.
The dry season for Koh Rong and the southern beaches, with calm, clear water.
The wet months, when the moats are full, the rice is vivid and the crowds thin out.
Skip April and early May, the hottest, most draining time across the country.

whatsOn.p: Cool, clear mornings make this the prime window for Angkor.
Bon Om Touk fills Phnom Penh with boat races as the rivers reverse their flow.

name: United States
lead: For most of the country, May, June, September and October are the window you want. Summer is peak in the north and the parks, winter suits Florida and the desert, and late summer brings heat and storms.

bestFor.p: Late September into October across New England and the northern states, when the maples turn and the air is crisp.
June to September, when high-country roads and trails are open and the weather is reliably warm. Book far ahead for the marquee parks.
Winter and spring for Florida and the Gulf, before the summer heat and hurricane risk arrive.
May, June, September and October for New York, Chicago and Boston, with mild days and long evenings.

whatsOn.p: New England and the Appalachians blaze red and gold, drawing leaf-peepers up the back roads.
Cities light up for the holidays, with skating rinks and markets despite the cold.

name: Canada
lead: Go in summer, June to August, for the warmest weather and longest days, or in September and October for autumn colour and fewer crowds. November to March is long and cold, but it is ski and northern-lights season.

bestFor.p: June to early September, when the weather is warm, the patios are open and the days are long.
Late September and October, especially in Quebec and Ontario, with crisp air and golden maples.
December to March for the Rockies and the best chance of northern lights in the north.
May and September offer mild weather and better prices than the July to August peak.

whatsOn.p: Maple country turns red and orange, at its best in Quebec and Ontario.
Whistler and the Rockies fill with snow and skiers through the long winter.

name: Mexico
lead: Go in the dry season, November to April, for sunny, comfortable days. The rainy season runs May to October, with afternoon storms, and the Caribbean coast watches the hurricane season, June to November.

bestFor.p: December to April on both coasts, with warm, dry, sunny weather, though prices peak over the winter holidays.
November to April for Mexico City, Oaxaca and the Yucatan, with comfortable temperatures for exploring.
Late October into early November, one of the country's most striking and atmospheric celebrations.
June offers a window of cheaper travel before the worst of the storm season, with greener landscapes.

whatsOn.h: Day of the Dead, early November
whatsOn.p: Marigolds, altars and processions fill towns from Oaxaca to Mexico City around 1 and 2 November.
The coasts are at their sunniest and driest from December through spring.

name: Brazil
lead: For Rio and the south, the cooler, drier months of April to June and September to October are the most comfortable. Summer, December to March, is hot and humid, and the season of Carnival and the beaches.

bestFor.p: December to March for hot summer beach days and Carnival, or the milder shoulders for easier sightseeing.
February or early March, when Rio and Salvador host the world's most famous street party.
June to October, the drier season, for wildlife spotting and more comfortable jungle travel.
Pleasant year round, with the falls fullest after the summer rains and the shoulder months most comfortable.

whatsOn.p: Rio and Salvador erupt into days of parades, samba and street parties.

whatsOn.h: Summer beach season, Dec to Mar
whatsOn.p: Rio's beaches are at their hottest and liveliest under the high summer sun.

name: Argentina
lead: For Buenos Aires and the centre, go in spring, September to November, or autumn, March to May. Patagonia is a summer trip, December to March. The seasons run opposite the northern hemisphere.

bestFor.p: September to November and March to May, when the city is at its most comfortable and the jacarandas bloom in spring.
December to March, the southern summer, when the trails are open and the fierce winds are at their gentlest.
March for the grape harvest, or the warm, dry autumn that follows it.
Comfortable much of the year, with the milder shoulder months easiest and the falls fullest after summer rains.

whatsOn.p: Mendoza celebrates the vendimia, the grape harvest, with festivals beneath the Andes.
Buenos Aires turns purple as the jacaranda trees flower across the city.

name: Peru
lead: For the Andes and Machu Picchu, go in the dry season, May to September, when skies are clear and trails are open. The wet season, November to March, brings rain and cloud, and the Inca Trail closes each February.

bestFor.p: May to September, the dry season, with the clearest skies and most reliable trails. June to August is the busy peak.
May to September for the firmest, driest conditions. Note that the trail closes every February, so plan around it.
December to March, the coastal summer, when the grey lifts and the beaches warm up.
The shoulder months of April, May, September and October offer good weather with thinner trails than midsummer.

whatsOn.p: Cusco stages the great Inca festival of the sun on 24 June, the highlight of the highland calendar.
Clear blue Andean skies make this the prime window for Machu Picchu and trekking.

name: Chile
lead: For Santiago and the wine country, go in spring, September to November, or autumn, March to May. Patagonia is a summer trip, December to March, and the Atacama Desert is good all year. The seasons are flipped from the northern hemisphere.

bestFor.p: December to March, the southern summer, for the W trek and Torres del Paine with the longest days.
September to November and March to May for the city and the vineyards in spring bloom or autumn harvest.
Year round, with the desert's clear skies among the best on the planet for stars.
June to September in the Andes near Santiago, when the northern hemisphere is in summer.

whatsOn.p: The valleys around Santiago celebrate the vendimia under the autumn sun.
The southern trails open under long days and calmer winds.

name: Colombia
lead: Go in the drier months, December to March, for the sunniest weather on the Caribbean coast and in the cities. On the equator there is no true summer or winter, just wetter and drier spells, with altitude setting the temperature.

bestFor.p: December to March for the sunniest, driest days in Cartagena, the beaches and Tayrona park.
The drier windows of December to February and July for Bogota, Medellin and the coffee region.
July to October on the Pacific coast, when humpback whales come to breed.
The drier months for clearer mountain views and firmer trails.

whatsOn.h: Caribbean dry season, Dec to Mar
whatsOn.p: Cartagena and the coast enjoy their sunniest, driest stretch.
Humpback whales gather along the Pacific coast to breed.

name: Costa Rica
lead: Go in the dry season, December to April, for the sunniest weather and easiest travel. The green season, May to November, brings warm afternoon rains, cheaper stays and dripping, vivid forests. The Caribbean coast runs to its own rhythm.

bestFor.p: December to April on the Pacific for sunny, dry days, with the green season bringing bigger surf and fewer crowds.
The green season, when the forests are dense and alive with wildlife, or the dry season for easier access and clearer trails.
July to October at Tortuguero on the Caribbean coast, when green turtles come ashore.
May, June and the green season for better rates, fewer crowds and vivid, green landscapes.

whatsOn.p: Green turtles nest on the Caribbean beaches of Tortuguero through the late summer.
The Pacific coast is at its sunniest and driest, prime time for the beaches.

name: Cuba
lead: Go in the dry season, November to April, for warm, sunny days in Havana and on the beaches. The wet season, May to October, is hotter and more humid, and overlaps the Caribbean hurricane season, which peaks from August to October.

bestFor.p: November to April for warm, dry, comfortable days exploring the old town and the classic-car streets.
December to April for Varadero, Cayo Coco and the keys at their sunniest and calmest.
The dry season for the clearest water around the reefs and the Bay of Pigs.
May and June, before the worst of the storms, for cheaper travel and greener landscapes.

whatsOn.p: The coast and keys enjoy their sunniest, calmest weather.
Music and parades fill the streets despite the summer heat.

name: Australia
lead: For Sydney and the south, go in spring, September to November, or autumn, March to May. The tropical north is best in its dry season, May to October. Remember the seasons are reversed: summer is December to February.

bestFor.p: June to October, the dry season, with clear water, calm seas and lower humidity. It also sits outside the worst of the stinger season.
December to February for warm summer days, or March to May for swimming with thinner crowds.
April to September, when the desert heat eases to comfortable days and crisp, cold nights.
March to May, when Melbourne, Adelaide and the wine regions glow in the autumn harvest.

whatsOn.p: Humpbacks migrate along the east and west coasts, easily spotted from headlands and boats.

whatsOn.h: Summer and festivals, Dec to Feb
whatsOn.p: Beach season peaks and the cities fill with open-air festivals and cricket.

name: New Zealand
lead: Go in summer, December to March, for the warmest weather and longest days, or in autumn, March to May, for golden colour and fewer crowds. Winter, June to August, is ski season in the Southern Alps.

bestFor.p: December to March, when the high trails are open, snow-free and the weather is at its kindest.
December to February for warm seas and the long, light summer evenings.
April and May, when Central Otago and Wanaka turn gold and the crowds thin out.
July to September around Queenstown, Wanaka and the central North Island volcanoes.

whatsOn.p: Central Otago and the southern lakes blaze with colour against the mountains.
The Southern Alps fill with snow for some of the southern hemisphere's best skiing.

name: Hungary
lead: Go in April to June or September to October for mild weather and thinner crowds in Budapest. Summer is warm and packed with festivals, and winter is cold but cosy, ideal for the city's famous thermal baths.

bestFor.p: April to June and September to October for mild days and lighter crowds along the Danube.
Year round, but best in winter, when steam rises off the warm outdoor pools.
Summer, peaking with the week-long Sziget festival on a Danube island in August.
September and October for the Tokaj and Eger harvests in the golden countryside.

whatsOn.p: One of Europe's biggest music festivals takes over an island in the Danube.
The steaming outdoor pools of Szechenyi are at their most atmospheric in the cold.

name: Denmark
lead: Go in summer, June to August, for the longest, mildest days, harbour swimming and Copenhagen at its most alive. Spring and autumn are quieter shoulders, and winter is dark and cold but full of hygge and Christmas lights.

bestFor.p: June to August for warm, long days, harbour swimming and the buzzing outdoor scene.
Summer for the gardens in full bloom, or December for the Christmas season.
Late spring to early autumn for the flat, easy cycling and the beaches.
Autumn and winter, for cosy candlelit cafes, design museums and better rates.

whatsOn.p: Copenhagen lives outdoors, with harbour baths and late, light evenings.
The historic gardens glow with lights and festive markets.

name: Finland
lead: Go in summer, June to August, for the midnight sun, lakes and endless forests, or in winter, December to March, for the northern lights, husky safaris and Santa in Lapland. The south is dark and cold in deep winter.

bestFor.p: December to March in Lapland, for the aurora, husky sledding and the Arctic winter wonderland.
June to August for cabin life, swimming, sauna and the endless northern light.
December in Rovaniemi, Santa's official hometown on the Arctic Circle.
September, when the northern forests turn red and gold in the ruska season.

whatsOn.p: The far north basks in near round-the-clock daylight for cabin and lake life.
The aurora glows over Lapland's snowy forests on clear nights.

name: Taiwan
lead: Go in autumn, October to November, or spring, March to April, for mild, dry days and clear skies. Summer is hot, humid and typhoon-prone, and winter is mild but often wet and grey in the north.

bestFor.p: October to November and March to April for mild, dry days exploring Taipei and Tainan.
Autumn and spring for clear skies and comfortable hiking in the high country.
The cooler months from autumn to early spring, when a soak in Beitou or Jiaoxi is most welcome.
Winter and spring in Kenting, when the south stays warm and sunny while the north is grey.

whatsOn.p: The post-summer skies clear for the mountains and the cities at their best.
Blossom opens in the hills around Taipei and Alishan from late winter into spring.

name: Dominican Republic
lead: Go from December to April, the drier, cooler season, for the best beach and resort weather in Punta Cana and beyond. The wetter months, May to November, are hotter and overlap the Caribbean hurricane season, which peaks from August to October.

bestFor.p: December to April for Punta Cana and the east at their sunniest, driest and calmest.
January to March in Samana Bay, when humpback whales come to breed offshore.
The windier winter months around Cabarete on the north coast.
Late spring and early summer, before the worst of the storm season, when prices drop.

whatsOn.p: Humpback whales gather in Samana Bay to breed and calve.
The east coast resorts enjoy their sunniest, calmest weather.

name: Fiji
lead: Go in the dry season, May to October, for sunny, slightly cooler weather and calm seas across the islands. The wet season, November to April, is hotter and more humid and overlaps the South Pacific cyclone season.

bestFor.p: May to October for the sunniest, driest, calmest weather across the Mamanucas and Yasawas.
The dry season for the clearest water and calmest seas on the famous soft-coral reefs.
Roughly April to October, when the southern swells bring the best waves to Fiji's breaks.
The wet season, for better rates and warm water, accepting the higher rain and cyclone risk.

whatsOn.p: Sunny, calm weather makes this the prime time for the island resorts.
Clear, calm water opens up Fiji's celebrated soft-coral reefs.

name: Papua New Guinea
lead: Go in the dry season, June to October, when Port Moresby and the south coast see barely any rain and the Highlands festivals fill August and September. The wet season, December to April, brings heavy rain to most of the country.

bestFor.p: August for the Mount Hagen Show, September for Goroka's, the Pacific's greatest gatherings of tribes and dress.
June to October for the Kokoda Track and Highlands walks, when the mud is at its most forgiving.
Year round in Milne Bay and Kimbe Bay; many divers rate the shoulder months either side of the dry season.
The dry season, when display trees are active and forest trails are passable at dawn.

whatsOn.p: Mount Hagen and Goroka: hundreds of tribes in full dress, dancing in one arena.
Port Moresby's rain all but stops, and the trekking and travel season opens.

name: Maldives
lead: Go in the dry season, December to April, for sunny skies, calm seas and the best diving and snorkelling. The wet season, May to November, is hotter and windier with more rain, but it brings cheaper stays, fewer crowds and the best surf.

bestFor.p: December to April for the sunniest skies, calmest lagoons and the classic postcard weather.
The dry season for the clearest water, though manta and whale sharks can be found year round around the right atolls.
May to October, when the southwest monsoon sends the best swell to the Maldivian breaks.
The wet season, May to November, for much lower resort prices and fewer crowds.

whatsOn.p: Calm lagoons and clear skies make this the prime time for the overwater villas.
Mantas and whale sharks gather around the atolls, the hotspots shifting with the monsoon.

name: Vanuatu
lead: Go in the dry season, May to October, for mild, settled weather, the clearest diving and the surest trips to the Mount Yasur volcano rim. The wet season, November to April, is hot and humid, and Vanuatu is one of the Pacific's most cyclone-exposed countries.

bestFor.p: May to October, when dry trails and clearer skies make the Yasur rim at dusk most reliable.
The dry season for visibility on the Coolidge and Santo's reefs, in warm water year round.
April to June for Pentecost Island's land diving, the original bungee, on towers of vine and wood.
November to April, accepting heat, rain and cyclone-season flexibility for quiet resorts and green islands.

whatsOn.h: Naghol land diving, Apr to Jun
whatsOn.p: Pentecost Islanders leap from wooden towers with vines at their ankles, a ritual for the yam harvest.
Mild trade-wind weather, the year's best for volcano trips, diving and island hopping.

name: Tuvalu
lead: Go from June to September, the drier trade-wind months, for calmer seas and the clearest water in Funafuti's lagoon. The wet season, November to April, brings heavy downpours, king tides and the South Pacific cyclone season.

bestFor.p: June to September, when the trade winds settle the water and visibility peaks.
The airstrip doubles as Funafuti's evening common: football, volleyball and picnics on the runway at dusk. Best in the dry months.
Any month. Tuvalu sees only a few thousand visitors a year, fewer than almost anywhere on Earth.
Everything stops on Sunday, year round. Slow down with it, and cover shoulders and knees in the villages.

whatsOn.p: Trade winds, calmer seas and the clearest lagoon water of the year.
Parades, feasting and dancing for Tuvalu Day close out the dry season.

name: Samoa
lead: Go in the dry season, May to October, for trade winds, sunshine and less than half the rain of high summer. The wet season, November to April, is hotter and much wetter and overlaps the South Pacific cyclone season.

bestFor.p: May to October, for sun, settled seas and comfortable nights in an open fale.
The dry season, when calm water clears up the lagoons and the To Sua trench.
Early September for the Teuila Festival, still inside the dry season.
The wet season, accepting daily downpours for green landscapes and quiet fales.

whatsOn.p: A week of fautasi longboat racing, dance and the crowning of Miss Samoa in Apia.
Trade winds and the year's most reliable sunshine across both islands.

name: Tonga
lead: Go in the dry season, May to October: mild, breezy and the driest weather of the year. From July to October humpback whales fill the islands, and Tonga is one of the few places on Earth where you can swim with them.

bestFor.p: July to October, with licensed operators out of Vava'u, Ha'apai and Tongatapu. Book months ahead.
The dry season, for steady trade winds and settled anchorages around Vava'u.
May to October. The water is coolest in August, so whale swimmers often wear a spring suit.
November to April, outside whale season, when rates drop and the islands go quiet.

whatsOn.p: Humpbacks calve in the sheltered waters, with mothers and calves resting near the surface.
Tonga's national festival: parades, dance and feasting around the king's birthday.

name: Solomon Islands
lead: Go from June to September, the drier trade-wind months, for the calmest seas and the clearest water over the reefs and WWII wrecks. The wet season, November to April, is hotter, stickier and much wetter, with some cyclone risk.

bestFor.p: June to September for the calmest seas and best visibility, in bathwater year round.
The dry months make Guadalcanal's battlefield sites and memorials easiest to reach. August marks the 1942 landings.
November to April, when north swells reach the breaks around Gizo and Santa Isabel.
The drier mid-year months, for trails that are merely muddy rather than flooded.

whatsOn.p: The steadiest weather of the year for diving, transfers and village travel.
Commemorations of the 1942 landings at the memorials above Honiara.

name: Kiribati
lead: Go from roughly June to October, the drier trade-wind months on Tarawa. Kiribati sits on the equator, so there is no cyclone season at all, but rainfall swings hard between El Nino and La Nina years, so treat every average loosely.

bestFor.p: Year round on Kiritimati's flats, one of the sport's great destinations, with calm dawn tides the daily rhythm.
Tarawa's battle sites and relics, easiest to walk in the drier mid-year months.
June to October, when the trades steady the water. It is warm, around 29 degrees, every month.
Kiribati is the first country to see each new day, and greeted the millennium first at aptly renamed Millennium Island.

whatsOn.p: The drier, breezier half of the year on Tarawa and the Gilberts.
A week of dancing, canoe racing and feasting across the atolls.

name: New Caledonia
lead: Go from September to December, when the islands are at their driest and spring warmth returns to the world's largest lagoon. June to August is dry but cool, and the hot, wetter season from January to March carries the cyclone risk.

bestFor.p: September to December, when the water warms back past 24 degrees under the year's driest skies.
Year round on the barrier reef, with the calmest, clearest conditions September to December.
July to September, when humpbacks shelter in the southern lagoon.
The cool, dry winter, June to September, for Grande Terre's ranges and the Great South.

whatsOn.p: Humpbacks gather in the southern lagoon, with boat trips out of Noumea and Prony.
The driest stretch of the year, with summer warmth returning to the lagoon.

name: French Polynesia
lead: Go in the dry season, May to October, for mild trade winds, low rain and the lagoons at their clearest, with July and August the driest months. The wet season, November to April, is hotter, stickier and much wetter, wettest around December.

bestFor.p: May to October for the surest sun. Book far ahead for July and August.
Year round in 26 to 29 degree water; the dry season has the calmest seas, and humpbacks pass August to October.
The big southern swells hit Teahupo'o May to October; gentler reef breaks run all year.
November to April, when resort rates ease and the islands turn green, accepting bursts of heavy rain.

whatsOn.p: A month of dance, drumming and outrigger racing, the biggest festival in the South Pacific.
Humpbacks cruise past Tahiti and Moorea, with regulated swim encounters on offer.

name: Singapore
lead: Singapore is hot and humid all year, so any time works. The slightly drier, brighter window is February to April, while the wettest months arrive with the monsoon from November to January.

bestFor.p: February to April for the brightest, driest spell, though the indoor sights make any month comfortable.
The drier months for Gardens by the Bay, the Botanic Gardens and Sentosa without the heaviest rain.
Year round, with Chinese New Year in late January or February among the liveliest times.
The mid-year Great Singapore Sale and the September Grand Prix weekend draw big crowds.

whatsOn.h: Chinese New Year, Jan or Feb
whatsOn.p: Chinatown and the city light up for the lunar new year celebrations.
The night race lights up Marina Bay for one of the sporting calendar's standout weekends.

name: Micronesia
lead: Aim for January to March, the least-wet months, for the ruins of Nan Madol, the wreck diving of Chuuk Lagoon and Yap's manta season. There is no true dry season here: Pohnpei is one of the rainiest places on Earth, so pack for showers whenever you come.

bestFor.p: Year round in the sheltered lagoon, with the calmest surface weather December to April.
December to April, when mantas crowd the cleaning stations in the channels.
January to March, when the reef flats and forest paths are at their least sodden.
October to April, when north swells light up Palikir Pass.

whatsOn.p: Yap's resident mantas gather at the channel cleaning stations.
The least-wet stretch of the year across the eastern states.

name: Marshall Islands
lead: Go from January to March, the driest months, when northeast trades keep the lagoons calm for diving and boat trips. September to November is the wettest stretch, and it is hot, humid and shower-prone the whole year round.

bestFor.p: December to April, for calm lagoons, better visibility and comfortable boat crossings.
Year round for tuna and reef species, with the calm early months easiest on small boats.
January to March, when trades are steady and outer-atoll boat runs are at their most reliable.
Any month. The Marshalls see only a few thousand visitors a year.

whatsOn.p: The driest, steadiest months, with January to March the pick.
Calm early-year water opens up the wrecks and islet picnic runs.

name: Palau
lead: Go from December to April, the drier northeast-trade months, for the calmest seas and peak visibility at Blue Corner and the Rock Islands. June to October is the wet season, with June and July the wettest months of all.

bestFor.p: December to April for calm seas and the best visibility, with manta season at German Channel peaking December to March.
The drier months, for settled water on the lagoon and camping-permit trips.
Jellyfish Lake and the Milky Way run year round; the dry season gives the clearest water.
June to October, when rooms and boats go quiet, accepting daily heavy showers.

whatsOn.p: Mantas stack up at German Channel's cleaning stations during the dry trades.
February to April are the driest months, with the calmest lagoon of the year.

name: Nauru
lead: Go from June to September, the driest months, when northeast trades take the edge off the equatorial heat. Nauru sits almost on the equator, so there are no cyclones, and like its neighbours its rainfall swings with El Nino years.

bestFor.p: Any month. For many visitors Nauru is the rarest stamp of all, and June to September is the comfortable window.
The dry months, for calmer water off the harbours and drop-offs metres from shore.
WWII relics and the phosphate workings, walkable year round; go early morning for the heat.
Noddies and frigatebirds over Topside and the coast, with locals still practising traditional frigatebird catching.

whatsOn.p: The year's least rain and steadiest trade winds.
Nauru's day of celebration, marking the survival and recovery of its people.

name: Cook Islands
lead: Go between June and October for the driest, breeziest weather, with September to November a warm, dry sweet spot before the rains. The damp season, December to March, is hotter and wetter and carries the cyclone risk.

bestFor.p: June to October for clarity and calm; Aitutaki day trips run year round.
July to October, when humpbacks pass close off Rarotonga's reef.
The dry months, when the red-earth trail over Rarotonga's spine is at its least slippery.
February to March, the quietest, wettest stretch, if you can live with humid heat and showers.

whatsOn.h: Te Maeva Nui, late Jul to early Aug
whatsOn.p: The constitution celebrations: two weeks of drumming and dance that pack Rarotonga.
Humpbacks cruise the reef edge, often visible from shore.

name: Niue
lead: Go in the dry season, May to October: cooler, drier, and from July to October humpback whales calve right off the reef. The wet season, November to April, is hotter and wetter and carries the cyclone risk.

bestFor.p: July to October, when humpbacks calve in Niue's deep, clear water, sometimes metres off the reef.
The dry season, for flat seas on the lee coast and that 50-metre-plus visibility.
May to October, when the sea tracks are dry underfoot and the pools are calm.
Any month. A couple of flights a week means Niue can never be crowded, and everything closes on Sundays.

whatsOn.p: Humpbacks rest and calve just off the reef, with strictly limited swim permits.
Cooler, drier days for the sea tracks, and the clearest water of the year.

name: Guam
lead: Go in the dry season, January to April, for reliable sun and the calmest reef conditions on Tumon Bay. July to November is the wet season and the heart of typhoon season, and Guam does take direct hits.

bestFor.p: January to April, for the surest sun on Tumon Bay's protected lagoon.
The dry season for calm, clear water, including the Blue Hole and double-war wrecks of Apra Harbor.
Year round: southern villages rotate patron-saint fiestas, and visitors are genuinely welcome.
The wet season, with resort deals balancing the daily showers and storm-watch caveats.

whatsOn.p: Trade winds, low rain and the calmest lagoon of the year.
Guam's biggest celebration: a month of fiestas ending in the Hagatna parade.
